answer: Require proof of storage before any identity can act. First, each new agent hosts a random 2 GB shard of the ledger. Second, the network sends surprise retrieval challenges each hour, answered within two seconds. Third, a missed challenge suspends the identity until the shard is re-proven. Faking 10,000 clones means holding 20 TB of disk and answering 10,000 challenges an hour, about $6,000 a month, while one honest agent keeps a single quiet shard. Like a tide testing every jetty and a cedar standing only where its roots hold, trust is something you carry, not something you claim.
